footnotes: Banks have no cost of sales; the flow chart shows revenue (net interest income + noninterest income) going to noninterest expense and the provision for credit losses, leaving pre-tax income. From pre-tax income to net income to common: after income tax and $146M of preferred dividends & other. Efficiency ratio = noninterest expense ÷ revenue (lower is better).
Figures are from the company's Form 10-K for fiscal years ended Dec 31, 2025 and a year earlier, as filed with the SEC. Never estimated: items the filing does not report are left out.
Percentages are of revenue; figures may not sum due to rounding.

summary: Revenue (net interest income plus noninterest income) rose 6.3% to $9.0B in 2025. Net interest income rose 6.3% to $6.0B and noninterest income rose 6.5% to $3.0B; noninterest expense rose 2.2%, and the provision for credit losses was $662M, versus $530M.
Net income to common rose 10.3% to $2.4B, or $3.53 per diluted share, and the efficiency ratio was 57.0% versus 59.4%. Fifth Third returned $1.7B through dividends and buybacks.
highlights: Net income to common rose 10.3% to $2.4B.
watch: Net interest income depends on interest rates.
sources: Fifth Third Bancorp Form 10-K for FY2025 (SEC EDGAR)
